newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland may soon pick investor for Celuloza - adviser.
newsitem.headline: Poland may soon pick investor for Celuloza - adviser.

text.p: Poland's treasury ministry may soon choose a strategic investor for the country's largest paper producer Zaklady Celulozy i Papieru Celuloza SA, a company advising the ministry on the sale said on Wednesday.
"Nothing has been decided yet, may be this (the choice of an investor) will take place in the coming days. Negotiations continue," Dariusz Olszewski, deputy president of the firm, told Reuters.

Newspapers have earlier reported that South Africa's Mondi and its Austrian subsidiary Frantschach AG have been picked as the investor in Celuloza, based in the northen city of Swiecie, but Olszewski declined to comment on the reports.
Celuloza's president Leopold Garbacz said on Tuesday that the company was keen on attracting a large firm from the paper sector as its strategic investor.
The treasury ministry wants to sell up to 65 percent of shares in Celuloza to a strategic investor and float 15 percent of its shares this month on the Warsaw bourse.

The public subscription for Celuloza's 7.5 million shares, with a minimum price of 15 zlotys each, is scheduled for April 15-18. The sale of tranche, representing 15 percent of the firm's capital, is due on April 22.
According to estimates, Celuloza netted 73 million zlotys last year on sales of 697.6 million zlotys.
In 1995 the company netted 110 million zloty on 760 million zloty revenues.
